steps: The record key selects a log partition.
Its leader appends the record at offset 42.
Followers replicate the ordered log according to acknowledgement policy.
Consumers fetch sequentially and persist their own progress.

lesson.scenario: An order producer appends to one replicated partition while a consumer group advances an offset.

steps.title: Stable partition
steps.narration: The replicated log ends at offset 1050 and billing has committed 1051.
steps.outcome: The consumer resumes from the stored next offset.
steps.invariant: Ordering is guaranteed within a partition, not across all partitions.

steps.title: Leader appends
steps.narration: The producer sends OrderPaid and the leader assigns offset 1051.
steps.outcome: The record has a durable position but is not yet committed.
steps.invariant: Only the partition leader assigns offsets in its epoch.

steps.title: Replication commits
steps.narration: The follower copies offsets 1051 and 1052; the high watermark advances.
steps.outcome: Consumers may fetch the committed prefix through 1052.
steps.invariant: Acknowledgement policy determines how many replicas must persist an append.

steps.title: Consumer processes batch
steps.narration: Billing fetches offsets 1051 and 1052 and applies their side effects.
steps.outcome: Processing is ahead of the stored group offset.
steps.invariant: A crash before offset commit may cause replay, so effects must tolerate duplicates.

steps.title: Offset committed
steps.narration: Billing commits next offset 1053 after successful processing.
steps.outcome: A restart resumes after the processed batch.
steps.invariant: Retention is independent of consumption; committed offsets are cursors, not deletions.
